page: Amazon Web Services c7g.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture, it features 2 dedicated physical cores using the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance allocates 4.0 GB of system memory, translating to 2.0 GB per core, and does not support hyperthreading. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1532.38, which is in the average tier, while the multi-core test yields 3043.08, placing it in the weak category. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 52.81 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 20.28 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression perform at an average tier of 24.18 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with clang fall into the weak to poor categories.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7g.large offers a low-overhead entry point into ARM-based compute environments, delivering dedicated physical cores without the resource sharing of burstable instances. However, the lack of local storage and modest memory capacity present tradeoffs for data-intensive tasks. This instance is suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, text processing, and simple utility scripts that benefit from dedicated ARM64 execution without requiring high memory density or parallel processing power.
